case_analysis.thread_summary: This thread covers both a quotation request for Bluetooth qualification and deeper technical validation of QDID combinations. The customer initially asks for cost and timeline estimates for RF PHY testing and listing. Later, they raise concerns about QDID combinations being rejected by another test house due to Consistency Check errors. The consultant analyzes the inter-layer inconsistencies and explains when qualification is still possible and when it is not. The discussion evolves into identifying a valid workaround using an appropriate Subset Design to enable successful qualification.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The core discussion focuses on QDID combination validity and handling of Inter-Layer Dependency (IDL) / Consistency Check errors. One scenario shows that even with IDL errors, qualification may still be possible under specific legacy or conditional rules. Another scenario highlights a hard failure case where Link Layer features (AoA/AoD) are not supported by the RF PHY, creating non-waivable inconsistencies. The consultant explains that such mismatches cannot be resolved via TCW and require selecting a compatible Subset DN. The role of ICS alignment and feature consistency across GAP, LL, and RF PHY layers is central to the qualification outcome.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant determines qualification feasibility by checking whether layer capabilities (ICS) are consistent across all included QDIDs. If inconsistencies exist but fall under acceptable legacy or conditional reuse scenarios, qualification may proceed. However, if inconsistencies involve mandatory feature mismatches that cannot be waived (e.g., AoA/AoD support mismatch), the design is invalid. The correct approach is to modify the design composition by selecting a compatible Subset DN that aligns all layer capabilities.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If incorrect QDID combinations are used, the project may fail during Consistency Check, leading to inability to register the product. This can cause delays due to redesign or re-selection of QDIDs and may require additional testing or re-submission. Attempting to force qualification using TCW where it is not allowed can result in rejection by the Bluetooth SIG. Misalignment between layers may also lead to repeated failures across different test houses, increasing cost and schedule risk.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always validate QDID combinations at the ICS and feature level across all layers before committing to a qualification path. Pay special attention to feature dependencies like AoA/AoD, as mismatches between Link Layer and RF PHY cannot be waived and require selecting a compatible Subset Design.
